Common Sense 250 Act of 2026

This bill requires the authorized monument honoring Thomas Paine to be located in Area 1 of the National Mall, which is reserved for commemorative works of preeminent historical and lasting significance to the United States. Thomas Paine was a philosopher and writer whose pamphlet, Common Sense, advocated for American independence from Great Britain.

items.summaryHtml:
Barona Group of Capitan Grande Band of Mission Indians Land Transfer Act of 2026

This bill takes three parcels of specified federal land (approximately 847 acres) in San Diego County, California, into trust for the benefit of the Barona Group of Capitan Grande Band of Mission Indians of the Barona Reservation, California. The land taken into trust shall be part of the Tribe's reservation.

One parcel (approximately 164 acres) is currently administered by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), and two parcels (approximately 683 acres) are currently administered by the Forest Service. Administrative jurisdiction over the Forest Service land must be transferred to the Department of the Interior.

Among other requirements, the bill requires the land taken into trust to remain subject to (1) existing liens, rights-of-way, reciprocal road rights-of-way agreements, licenses, leases, permits, special use permits, and easements; (2) continuing public access to the land, including roads and trails, as on the date of the bill's enactment; and (3) rights-of-way necessary for BLM and Forest Service employees to access the land for operational and emergency purposes (e.g., wildfire suppression).

The bill requires the Tribe to maintain the fuel break within two of the parcels in accordance with applicable Forest Service standards.

The bill prohibits gaming on the land taken into trust.

South Dakota Water Feasibility Studies Act

This bill directs the Department of the Interior to study the feasibility of constructing projects to supply municipal, rural, and industrial water from the Missouri River in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, and South Dakota. Specifically, the bill requires studies on projects to supply water to the (1) Western Dakota Regional Water System; (2) Lewis and Clark Regional Water System, Inc.; and (3) Dakota Mainstem Regional Water System.

Renewing the African American Civil Rights Network Act

This bill reauthorizes for seven years the African American Civil Rights Network. The network is a National Park Service (NPS) program that designates historical sites and educational resources that are connected to the African American civil rights movement. The program expired on January 8, 2025.

Locations, facilities, and resources included in the network are eligible to use the network logo and receive technical support from the NPS.

items.summaryHtml:
Earth MRI Reauthorization Act of 2026

This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative, a U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) program charged with integrating and modernizing the mapping of U.S. natural resources, with a focus on critical mineral resources such as lithium and titanium. The bill also expands the initiative’s data integration functions and requires the USGS to give preference to U.S. contractors under the initiative.

Specifically, the bill requires entities contracting with the USGS pursuant to the initiative to disclose the ownership of the primary contractor and each subcontractor carrying out a part of the contract. To the extent practicable, the USGS must give preference to entities owned and controlled in the United States when entering contracts under the initiative, while giving appropriate consideration to specialized expertise essential to the objectives of the initiative.

Further, under current law, the initiative is required to provide certain types of integrated mapping, including geologic, geophysical, and topographical mapping. Under the bill, the initiative must include data from the USGS 3D Hydrography Program, which maps U.S. water resources. The bill also explicitly allows the initiative’s integrated mapping to include data from modern sensing technologies, including real-time data acquisition systems and data-driven analytical methods.

items.summaryHtml:
Crossett Experimental Forest Act of 2026

This bill directs the Forest Service, upon the request of the State of Arkansas, to convey the Crossett Experimental Forest, the R.R. Reynolds Research Natural Area, and associated facilities to the state. 

Upon the conveyance, Arkansas must designate the land as the Crossett Experimental State Forest. In order to retain the land, Arkansas must

  • use the land for forest research, education, and demonstration purposes in a manner consistent with the historic research mission of the forest; and
  • use the forest in coordination with the University of Arkansas at Monticello and the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture, including by providing the universities with reasonable access to the forest for research and educational purposes.

The bill outlines the terms and conditions of the conveyance, including requiring the conveyance to be (1) subject to valid existing rights, (2) made without consideration (e.g., payment), and (3) made by quitclaim deed.

Arkansas must pay the costs of the conveyance, including costs for surveys and other administrative costs.

items.summaryHtml:
This bill exchanges administrative jurisdiction over specified parcels of federal land between Yosemite National Park and Stanislaus National Forest in California.

By way of background, cattle are grazing on the land currently managed by the National Park Service. However, grazing on federal lands primarily occurs on lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management or the Forest Service. The transfer would allow the land with cattle grazing to be managed by the Forest Service, which has a multiple-use management plan that is consistent with grazing.
